events.title: Scenario: Data-center electrification may be increasing substation load clusters
events.summary: Data-center electrical load growth may be concentrating stress on specific substations. That could create procurement and operational pressure if transformer lead times remain long.

events.title: Scenario: Limited sensor retrofits create diagnostic blind spots in aging substations
events.summary: Uneven sensor adoption in aging substations may leave diagnostic blind spots. Targeted retrofits would reduce detection latency but require procurement and deployment coordination.

events.title: Scenario: HVDC converter and specialty component lead times could extend project timelines
events.summary: Specialized HVDC component capacity constraints could extend project schedules and push developers toward modular or phased approaches.

events.title: Scenario: Shift toward modular substation solutions to manage lead-time and site complexity
events.summary: Modular substation adoption could mitigate schedule risk from long lead times and labor constraints but requires early technical alignment and possibly updated standards.

events.title: Scenario: On-site battery adoption in data centers could change peak interactions with distribution networks
events.summary: Data centers adopting behind-the-meter batteries could lower peaks but also create new charging-related stress on distribution assets without coordinated telemetry and dispatch.

events.title: Scenario: Rapid solar interconnection at distribution may increase localized congestion
events.summary: Distributed solar growth may create feeder-level constraints that require either control solutions or targeted reinforcement, shifting near-term procurement priorities toward smart inverters and voltage-control equipment.

events.title: Scenario: Trade frictions could increase volatility in critical-mineral availability for HV equipment
events.summary: Trade and logistics pressures may increase volatility in critical-mineral availability, affecting HV equipment manufacturing and project schedules.

events.title: Scenario: Capacity-market design shifts could favor flexible resources and change procurement demand
events.summary: Market design that prioritizes flexibility may redirect procurement from large fixed assets to fast-response technologies, with implications for manufacturers and grid operations.

events.title: Scenario: Faster AI forecasting adoption could reduce scheduled reserves but increase model-risk exposure
events.summary: AI forecasting may reduce scheduled reserves and operating costs but raises model-risk issues that require governance, redundancy, and clear fallback protocols to avoid negative reliability outcomes.

events.title: Scenario: New insulation materials and dry-type designs could shift manufacturing lines and safety profiles
events.summary: Demand for lower-fire-risk transformer designs could drive manufacturing shifts and qualification processes, altering availability and procurement strategies for substations.
